{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-ks-c","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"c66bdc6eb8d5cb2093f53fa25c4cb76ab1932018109691337c5238d623658b38","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-ks-class-c:lineage:32","source_registry_sha256":"c7fb2073a9e8bb6a73d0151458fe04991b703d84f882b00a01bedfcea433c383","source_liveness_sha256":"94328be42cc10cf86af8e486b41bc40c72c45e4700d27b9b46d1f3d2feac7bb6"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Safe driving","heading":"C — Safe driving","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Safe driving

FACT_ID: sec07-F01 | anchor: A56
A handbook cannot replace driving instruction and supervised practice needed to develop experience and judgment. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec07-F02 | anchor: A56
Scan ahead, beside and behind the vehicle to detect problems that may require a speed or position change. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec07-F03 | anchor: A56
Looking far along the intended path can reduce emergency reactions and steering weave while helping traffic flow steadily. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec07-F04 | anchor: A56
On a highway, the handbook recommends looking at least a quarter-mile ahead. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec07-F05 | anchor: A56
Search ahead for entering or turning vehicles and brake lights so speed or lane changes can be made early. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec07-F06 | anchor: A56
A light that has remained green for a long time may change before arrival; begin slowing and prepare to stop. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec07-F07 | anchor: A56
Early driving adjustments give following drivers more time to respond. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec07-F08 | anchor: A56
Measure look-ahead time by counting seconds until reaching a stationary object first seen ahead. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec07-F09 | anchor: A56
The handbook defines visual lead as the area about 20 to 30 seconds in front of the vehicle. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec07-F10 | anchor: A56
A useful visual lead helps identify changing conditions and alternative paths early enough to stop or steer. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec07-F11 | anchor: A57
With good tires and brakes on dry pavement, the handbook's 60-mph example allows about four to five seconds or 359 feet to react and stop. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec07-F12 | anchor: A57
Under the same stated good-tire, good-brake and dry-road conditions, its 30-mph example allows about two to three seconds or 123 feet to react and stop. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec07-F13 | anchor: A57
The handbook warns that 60 mph is too fast for visibility when the driver cannot see at least 400 feet ahead. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec07-F14 | anchor: A57
The handbook cautions that 30 mph may be unsafe when the visible distance is less than 150 feet. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec07-F15 | anchor: A57
Search sideways for vehicles and pedestrians entering the path, especially at intersections and railroad crossings. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec07-F16 | anchor: A57
Intersections include driveways, shopping-center lanes and parking-lot entrances as well as crossing streets. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec07-F17 | anchor: A57
On intersection approach, check traffic, road users, controls, blocked views and pavement conditions. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec07-F18 | anchor: A57
Before entering an intersection, search ahead, left and right; after stopping, look left, right and left again. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec07-F19 | anchor: A57
Check cross traffic even when it faces red or a stop sign, particularly immediately after the light turns green. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec07-F20 | anchor: A57
Enter an intersection only with a clear path through it and a view of crossing traffic, so a stop will not block it. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec07-F21 | anchor: A57
When stopped with a blocked cross-street view, edge forward slowly until the view opens. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec07-F22 | anchor: A57
Give extra sideways attention near busy sidewalks, shopping areas, construction, playgrounds and schoolyards. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec07-F23 | anchor: A57
Before a left turn across opposing traffic, find a safe gap and ensure vehicles or pedestrians will not block the turning path. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec07-F24 | anchor: A57
Before turning right, check traffic from the left, opposing left-turners and crossing pedestrians. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec07-F25 | anchor: A57
At a railroad approach, slow at the round warning sign and look both ways for trains or maintenance equipment before the tracks. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec07-F26 | anchor: A57
Check behind more often in heavy traffic to detect tailgaters and vehicles approaching too fast. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec07-F27 | anchor: A57
Rearward checks are particularly important before changing lanes, slowing, joining traffic or descending a long or steep hill. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec07-F28 | anchor: A58
Before a lane change or merge, check behind and in the target lane, including vehicles already entering it or preparing to pass. [A58]
Source: [A58 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec07-F29 | anchor: A58
Maintain safe following space while checking mirrors for a lane change. [A58]
Source: [A58 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec07-F30 | anchor: A58
A blind spot is an area the mirrors do not show; look over the shoulder toward the intended movement to check it. [A58]
Source: [A58 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec07-F31 | anchor: A58
Use repeated short checks instead of one long sideways look because traffic ahead may stop while attention is elsewhere. [A58]
Source: [A58 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec07-F32 | anchor: A58
For a lane change, signal, recheck toward the move, adjust speed and steer into the lane, then cancel the signal. [A58]
Source: [A58 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec07-F33 | anchor: A58
Check mirrors whenever slowing, especially suddenly or at a driveway or parking space where followers may not expect it. [A58]
Source: [A58 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec07-F34 | anchor: A58
On a long or steep descent, watch mirrors for rapidly approaching vehicles, especially large trucks and buses. [A58]
Source: [A58 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec07-F35 | anchor: A58
Perception distance is the distance traveled from seeing a hazard until recognizing it under ideal conditions. [A58]
Source: [A58 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec07-F36 | anchor: A58
Visibility, the hazard and a driver's mental or physical condition can change perception distance. [A58]
Source: [A58 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec07-F37 | anchor: A58
The handbook gives an alert driver's average perception time as three quarters of a second to one second. [A58]
Source: [A58 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec07-F38 | anchor: A58
Reaction distance is the ideal-condition distance traveled before physically applying the brakes in response to a recognized hazard. [A58]
Source: [A58 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec07-F39 | anchor: A58
The handbook gives average reaction time as three quarters of a second to one second and illustrates about 55 feet traveled at 50 mph. [A58]
Source: [A58 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec07-F40 | anchor: A58
Braking distance is the distance traveled while the brakes are being applied under ideal conditions. [A58]
Source: [A58 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec07-F41 | anchor: A58
The handbook's 50-mph dry-road example with good brakes gives about 158 feet of braking distance. [A58]
Source: [A58 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec07-F42 | anchor: A58
Total stopping distance combines perception, reaction and braking travel until the vehicle fully stops. [A58]
Source: [A58 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec07-F43 | anchor: A58
For its ideal-condition 50-mph example, the handbook gives a minimum total stopping distance of 268 feet. [A58]
Source: [A58 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0058]

Misconceptions: Mirrors leave blind spots; a green signal does not prove a clear path; ABS does not promise a shorter dry-road stop; another driver's signal does not guarantee a turn.
Mnemonics: Editorial cue: search, assess, choose, act. The cue summarizes the decision sequence without adding a rule.
Glossary: Visual lead, perception distance, reaction distance, braking distance, hydroplaning, ABS, ESP and space cushion are defined in the sourced blocks.
Dynamic facts: Numeric examples are bound to this edition and their stated conditions; legal requirements, equipment behavior and unresolved timing ranges need issuer or vehicle-manual rechecking.

FACT_ID: sec07-F44 | anchor: A59
The handbook compares 40 mph with 20 mph as four times the impact and braking distance, illustrating the effect of increased speed. [A59]
Source: [A59 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec07-F45 | anchor: A59
Its 60-mph comparison with 20 mph gives nine times the impact and braking distance. [A59]
Source: [A59 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec07-F46 | anchor: A59
Its 80-mph comparison with 20 mph gives sixteen times the impact and braking distance. [A59]
Source: [A59 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec07-F47 | anchor: A59
Sudden slowing makes it harder for following vehicles to avoid a collision. [A59]
Source: [A59 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec07-F48 | anchor: A59
To avoid panic stops, the handbook recommends searching at least ten seconds ahead and making needed changes early. [A59]
Source: [A59 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec07-F49 | anchor: A59
Planning ahead and slowing gradually can conserve fuel. [A59]
Source: [A59 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec07-F50 | anchor: A59
Choose speed for traffic and road conditions, available forward view, following space and applicable limits. [A59]
Source: [A59 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec07-F51 | anchor: A59
Reduce speed before sharp curves, on slippery pavement and when animals may be on the road. [A59]
Source: [A59 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec07-F52 | anchor: A59
Slow to a safe speed before a curve rather than braking hard after entry, which can cause loss of traction. [A59]
Source: [A59 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec07-F53 | anchor: A59
Reduce curve-entry speed further when traction is poor, when following another vehicle or when the curve's end is hidden. [A59]
Source: [A59 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec07-F54 | anchor: A59
At a safe curve speed, the handbook calls for slight, steady acceleration through the curve. [A59]
Source: [A59 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec07-F55 | anchor: A59
Slow at the first signs of rain, snow or sleet because water mixes with dirt and oil to make the surface slippery. [A59]
Source: [A59 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec07-F56 | anchor: A59
A sudden rain on hot pavement may be particularly slippery during the first few minutes before surface oil washes away. [A59]
Source: [A59 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec07-F57 | anchor: A59
Poor grip on wet pavement lengthens stops and makes skid-free turning harder. [A59]
Source: [A59 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec07-F58 | anchor: A59
For wet roads, the handbook recommends about 10 mph below the recommended speed to allow extra stopping and steering space. [A59]
Source: [A59 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec07-F59 | anchor: A59
For packed snow, the handbook recommends reducing speed by at least half. [A59]
Source: [A59 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec07-F60 | anchor: A59
On ice, reduce speed to provide extra stopping and recovery room; avoid driving on ice-covered roads if possible. [A59]
Source: [A59 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec07-F61 | anchor: A59
The handbook permits studded snow tires in Kansas from November 1 through April 1. [A59]
Source: [A59 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec07-F62 | anchor: A59
A road's crown and drainage slope can carry a skidding vehicle toward the roadside. [A59]
Source: [A59 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec07-F63 | anchor: A60
Shaded pavement on cold wet days can freeze before other areas and dry later. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec07-F64 | anchor: A60
Bridge, overpass and underpass pavement may be icy even when nearby roads are clear. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec07-F65 | anchor: A60
Near freezing, liquid water over ice can make the surface more slippery than ice at much colder temperatures. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec07-F66 | anchor: A60
Hydroplaning occurs when tires ride on pooled water and lose contact with the pavement. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec07-F67 | anchor: A60
Slow in rain and on wet roads with puddles to reduce hydroplaning risk. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec07-F68 | anchor: A60
Driving faster than the traffic stream creates repeated passing conflicts; keep pace within legal limits. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec07-F69 | anchor: A60
The handbook warns that driving over 15 mph below the traffic stream can create dangerous bunching and passing attempts. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec07-F70 | anchor: A60
If traffic bunches behind a slow vehicle, its driver should pull over when safe and let others pass. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec07-F71 | anchor: A60
On an entrance ramp, check destination and route signs and obey ramp-speed signs. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec07-F72 | anchor: A60
Use an acceleration lane to approach traffic speed before joining the main roadway. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec07-F73 | anchor: A60
Avoid reaching the end of an acceleration lane and stopping; if a gap is unavailable, slow within the lane while waiting. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec07-F74 | anchor: A60
Do not cross the solid white boundary when joining from an acceleration lane. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec07-F75 | anchor: A60
Before joining the roadway, check mirrors and over the shoulder toward the move; signal and enter carefully when a gap opens. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec07-F76 | anchor: A60
In heavy traffic, the handbook recommends reaching the exit lane about half a mile before the exit. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec07-F77 | anchor: A61
For an exit with a deceleration lane, maintain speed on the main roadway and reduce it after entering that lane. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec07-F78 | anchor: A61
When exiting a limited-access road, check the ramp speed and following traffic before slowing, and brake with regard to vehicles ahead. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec07-F79 | anchor: A61
Reduce speed in crowded places where maneuvering room is limited, including shopping areas and busy downtown streets. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec07-F80 | anchor: A61
Heavy rush-hour traffic, narrow bridges, tunnels and toll plazas can require lower speed for limited space and changing movements. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec07-F81 | anchor: A61
Near schools, playgrounds and residential streets, watch for children entering the road unexpectedly. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec07-F82 | anchor: A61
At railroad crossings, check for trains and room to clear; uneven crossing levels may require slowing. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec07-F83 | anchor: A61
Excess speed reduces maneuvering ability and increases the distance traveled while reacting. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec07-F84 | anchor: A61
Higher speed can reduce barrier protection and increase collision severity. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec07-F85 | anchor: A61
The handbook identifies added tire and brake wear, driver fatigue and harder distance judgments by others as speed-related risks. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec07-F86 | anchor: A61
For normal conditions without special hazards or a different posted limit, the handbook gives 30 mph for an urban district. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec07-F87 | anchor: A62
A posted speed assumes ideal conditions; slow for wet or icy pavement, poor visibility or heavy traffic. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec07-F88 | anchor: A62
A posted 55-mph limit does not make 55 mph appropriate during a snowstorm. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec07-F89 | anchor: A62
Check the speedometer frequently, especially after moving from a fast multilane road to a slower road. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec07-F90 | anchor: A62
High-center-of-gravity vehicles are more prone to rollover; drive at a suitable lower speed, avoid abrupt direction changes and slow before curves. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec07-F91 | anchor: A62
ABS means Anti-Lock Braking System and is intended to permit steering while braking without upsetting vehicle balance. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec07-F92 | anchor: A62
ABS does not necessarily shorten dry-road stops, though the handbook says it generally shortens wet-surface stops. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec07-F93 | anchor: A62
For ABS use, the handbook directs the driver to find open space, press the brake firmly and steer toward that space. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec07-F94 | anchor: A62
Use the owner's manual to establish whether a vehicle has ABS. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec07-F95 | anchor: A62
The ABS indicator normally illuminates at startup and then goes out; a light that stays on indicates a malfunction. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec07-F96 | anchor: A62
ESP means Electronic Stability Program; it compares the driver's steering request with the vehicle's actual movement. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec07-F97 | anchor: A62
ESP can apply individual brakes when it detects a traction-related mismatch to help reduce skidding. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec07-F98 | anchor: A62
During traction loss with ESP, steer toward the intended path and avoid abrupt steering. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec07-F99 | anchor: A62
A space cushion gives more time to react to other road users. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec07-F100 | anchor: A62
The handbook specifies a two-second minimum following interval, adding a second for unusual traffic or weather conditions. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec07-F101 | anchor: A63
Check following time by counting from when the vehicle ahead clears a fixed marker until the following vehicle reaches it; fewer than two seconds is too close. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec07-F102 | anchor: A63
If following too closely, slow down and repeat the fixed-marker count until the interval is at least two seconds. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec07-F103 | anchor: A63
Slippery roads may require more than the basic two-second following interval. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec07-F104 | anchor: A63
When a following driver wants to pass, slow to create more room ahead and shorten the passing maneuver. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec07-F105 | anchor: A63
Leave extra space behind motorcycles for differing braking performance or a fallen rider. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec07-F106 | anchor: A63
Increase following space behind vehicles with blocked rear views so their drivers can see the following vehicle and its driver can see ahead. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec07-F107 | anchor: A63
Carry a larger front cushion when hauling a heavy load or towing a trailer because stopping takes longer and steering ability decreases. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec07-F108 | anchor: A63
Increase following space in darkness or bad weather that reduces the forward view. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec07-F109 | anchor: A63
When tailgated, increase the space ahead so braking or steering can be less abrupt. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec07-F110 | anchor: A63
Give emergency vehicles additional following space to operate. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec07-F111 | anchor: A63
Leave extra room behind vehicles that must stop at railroad crossings, such as buses and hazardous-material carriers. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec07-F112 | anchor: A63
Leave extra space when stopped behind another vehicle on an incline because it may roll backward before moving ahead. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec07-F113 | anchor: A63
Steady speed, early signals and extra front space before slowing can help a following driver maintain a safe gap. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0063]
